title: (BTP v_3) NEW Supplier Booking Search SEARCH_NAVIGATE
description: Starting from wherever the shared browser session already is (ideally the already-authenticated Bingtrip merchant portal handed off by the login bot), switches the interface to English, opens Hotels > Orders > Booking Manage, CLEARS EVERY FILTER FIELD, filters by booking ID, reads the matching order row off the page, then downloads that order's 'download confirmation slip' PDF (a 'Voucher' document) and parses the remaining fields out of it. Modeled on the (BAB v_7) Holiday supplier-booking-search workflow and keeping its block shape: a Browser Task checkpoint block (Find_Booking) reaches and reads the filtered row, a file_download block performs the download, a file_url_parser block extracts the voucher fields, and a code block merges both stages into the shared 14-field booking schema. Two-stage by design: the voucher PDF prints each value as a single non-wrapping line and truncates anything too long, so the hotel name, room type, stay dates, guest names, IBN and HCN are taken from the portal table (which wraps and shows full text) and only the address, hotel phone, bed configuration and meal plan come from the PDF. Guest count is not published by this portal, so adultCount is derived from the number of names listed in the order row's 'Guest / Contact Person' cell, duplicates included. v_1: initial version. v_2: renamed to the BTP series; ibn now comes from the hexadecimal Platform Booking ID (second line of the 'Booking ID / Platform Booking ID' cell), not the numeric Booking ID, with the voucher's own 'Booking No' as a fallback; the language check is now explicitly a no-op when the portal is already in English; the Download_Voucher goal was rewritten around the click itself after a run where that block reported success having performed only two actions and saved no file (Skyvern hard-sets complete_on_download=True on file_download blocks, which disables the completion-verification pass, so an early self-declared COMPLETE is never challenged), and it now also handles the case where the PDF opens in the browser's built-in viewer; a Check_Download code block was added between the download and the parser so an empty download fails with a readable message instead of the opaque 'Failed to format jinja template: Can't compile non template nodes' the file parser raises when it falls back to using the whole task-output dict as its file_url. v_3: Download_Voucher rewritten again after a run where the link WAS clicked and still no file was saved. Skyvern already waits for a download signal after a download-intent click and, when none arrives, hands the agent a follow-up telling it to keep trying rather than report the goal complete - but the v_2 prompt contradicted that signal by declaring an unchanged page to be success and forbidding a second click, so the agent completed anyway. The goal now states outright that the page cannot tell you whether a file was saved, that an uncredited download means NOT done, and gives a recovery ladder: check for a second tab (a PDF shown in the browser's own viewer is not a downloaded file, it has to be saved from the viewer toolbar), then one repeat click, then TERMINATE. max_steps_per_run raised to 15 to leave room for it, and download_suffix dropped so no post-download rename sits between the browser and the file the parser reads.

parameters.description: The Bingtrip order to look up, typed into the 'Booking ID' filter on the Orders > Booking Manage page. That field accepts either identifier shown in the table's 'Booking ID / Platform Booking ID' column: the numeric Booking ID (e.g. '8260902055928430') or the long hexadecimal Platform Booking ID (e.g. '5e977b32aaddd27f0be39daf2d0b8430').
The Bingtrip merchant portal homepage URL to start the run from.

blocks.label: Find_Booking
blocks.title: Find_Booking
blocks.navigation_goal:
*** OBJECTIVE: reach the point where the Orders > Booking Manage results table is filtered down to the single order '{{booking_id}}' and its row (including the 'download confirmation slip' link) is on screen ***

0. This block continues on whatever page the browser is already showing (it does not force a fresh navigation) — the browser session may already be sitting on the authenticated Bingtrip merchant portal from a prior login step. First check what is currently on screen:
   - If it is already the Bingtrip merchant portal (the blue header with the 'bingtrip' logo, a globe icon, 'USD', a mail icon and the account name on the right, and a left sidebar with 'Hotels', 'Settlement', 'Developer', 'Authorization', 'Settings'), do NOT reload or re-navigate to '{{website_url}}' — reloading a working authenticated page can needlessly discard client-side session state on this portal. Proceed directly to step 1 from the current page.
   - If the browser is on a blank page, a different site, or anything that is not the Bingtrip merchant portal, navigate to '{{website_url}}' once, then proceed to step 1.
1. CHECK THE INTERFACE LANGUAGE — and only act if it is NOT already English. Read the main content area of the current page:
   - IF everything readable is already in English: do nothing at all here. Do NOT open the language menu, do NOT click the globe icon — go straight to step 2. This is the normal case and it must cost zero actions.
   - ONLY IF Chinese text is visible (e.g. '目的地', '入住', '退房', '最近查看过的酒店'): click the globe/language icon in the top blue header bar (just to the right of the 'bingtrip' logo, past a thin vertical divider). A small dropdown opens with exactly three options — '简体中文', '繁體中文' and 'English', each with a small flag. Click 'English', wait for the page to re-render, then continue.
   Do not open the language menu again at any later point in this task.
2. In the left sidebar, open 'Hotels' if its sub-menu is collapsed (it expands to 'Explore', 'My collection', 'Orders'), then click 'Orders'.
   - IMPORTANT: click 'Orders', not 'Explore' and not 'My collection' — those are different sections.
3. Confirm you landed on the Orders page: two tabs are shown near the top, 'Booking Manage' and 'Portal'. 'Booking Manage' must be the active tab — if 'Portal' is active instead, click 'Booking Manage'.
   Below the tabs is a filter panel containing the fields 'Booking ID' (placeholder 'Booking ID/Platform Booking ID'), 'Hotel Name', 'Guest / Contact Person' (two boxes: 'Name' and 'Last Name'), 'Confirmation No', 'Order Status', 'Cost status', and 'Booking Date' (a 'Start date' → 'End date' range), plus a blue 'Search' button, a 'Reset' button and an 'expand' link.
4. *** CLEAR EVERY FILTER FIELD FIRST — THIS IS MANDATORY. *** The portal remembers filter values between visits (for example a 'Booking Date' start date such as '2026-09-01 00:00:00' is often left over from a previous session), and any leftover value silently narrows the search so the booking is reported as not found.
   - Click the 'Reset' button once and wait for the filter panel to re-render.
   - Then VISUALLY VERIFY that every single filter input is now empty and shows only its grey placeholder text: 'Booking ID', 'Hotel Name', 'Name', 'Last Name', 'Confirmation No', 'Order Status', 'Cost status', and both halves of the 'Booking Date' range ('Start date' and 'End date').
   - If ANY field still holds a value after Reset, clear that field by hand: click the small circled '⊗' clear icon that appears at the right edge of the field, or click into the field, select all of its text and delete it. Repeat until every field is empty.
   - Note: the filter panel may also carry additional fields shown via the 'expand' link. Do not click 'expand' yourself, but if extra filter fields are already visible, they must be empty too — clear them the same way.
5. Only once every filter field is confirmed empty, click into the 'Booking ID' field (the first field, placeholder 'Booking ID/Platform Booking ID') and type '{{booking_id}}' into it. Leave every other filter field empty — do not select anything in the 'Order Status' or 'Cost status' dropdowns and do not pick any 'Booking Date'.
6. Click the blue 'Search' button. Do NOT click 'Reset' again at this point (that would wipe the Booking ID you just typed).
7. Wait for the results table below to refresh. It should now contain exactly ONE order row, and the pager under the table should read 'Total 1 items'. The row's 'Booking ID / Platform Booking ID' cell holds two values on two lines: a numeric Booking ID on the first line and a long hexadecimal Platform Booking ID on the second — '{{booking_id}}' will match one of those two.
   - If the table shows zero rows / a 'No data' placeholder, or no row matches '{{booking_id}}', do not proceed further — this is a failure case handled by TERMINATE below.
   - If more than one row is returned, use only the row whose Booking ID or Platform Booking ID matches '{{booking_id}}' exactly.
8. The results table is WIDER than the visible area and has its own horizontal scrollbar just below the row. Drag that horizontal scrollbar to the right (or scroll the table sideways) until the right-hand columns — 'Confirmation No', 'Total Price', 'Order Status / Cost status', 'Cancellation Policy', 'Order Source' and 'Action' — are visible, and the blue 'download confirmation slip' link in the 'Action' column of the matching row is on screen.
   - Do NOT click 'download confirmation slip' in this block, and do NOT click the 'Export' button above the table — downloading is the job of the next step in this workflow, not this one.

If a cookie-consent banner, a notification popup or any other modal covers the page at any point, dismiss it and continue. If any click in this sequence lands somewhere unexpected (wrong menu, wrong tab, an error toast, the table not refreshing), do not treat that as final — re-orient from what is actually on screen and retry the step that went wrong instead of continuing forward from the wrong page.
blocks.data_extraction_goal:
Read the single order row currently shown in the Orders > Booking Manage results table (the row matching '{{booking_id}}') and return its values.

This page — not the downloadable voucher PDF — is the authoritative source for these particular fields, because the table cells wrap and show their full text, whereas the PDF prints each value as a single line that is cut off when it is too long.

The row's cells continue to the RIGHT beyond the visible area of the table; all of them belong to the same single row. The columns, left to right, are: 'Booking Date', 'Booking ID / Platform Booking ID', 'Hotel Name / Room Type', 'Check-In/Out / Room Night', 'Guest / Contact Person', 'Confirmation No', 'Total Price', 'Order Status / Cost status', 'Cancellation Policy', 'Order Source', 'Action'.

Read exactly these values from that one row:
- The long hexadecimal Platform Booking ID (the SECOND line of the 'Booking ID / Platform Booking ID' cell, e.g. '5e977b32aaddd27f0be39daf2d0b8430') — NOT the shorter numeric Booking ID printed on the first line.
- The hotel name (the FIRST line of the 'Hotel Name / Room Type' cell, e.g. 'Under Canvas Grand Canyon').
- The room type (the SECOND line of that same cell, e.g. 'Suite with Kids Tent - Private Bath').
- The check-in and check-out dates from the FIRST line of the 'Check-In/Out / Room Night' cell, printed as '<check-in> ~<check-out>' in YYYY-MM-DD form (e.g. '2026-09-19 ~2026-09-21').
- The guest names from the FIRST line of the 'Guest / Contact Person' cell — a comma-separated list such as 'DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel'. The SECOND line of that cell is a telephone number (e.g. '+13024077400') and is the contact person's phone, NOT a guest name — never include it among the names.
- The confirmation number from the 'Confirmation No' column (e.g. '32685SG107373').

Return exactly one object. If a value is genuinely absent from the row, output null for it — never invent one and never substitute a value from a different column.
blocks.complete_criterion: The Orders > Booking Manage results table shows exactly one order row whose 'Booking ID' or 'Platform Booking ID' value is '{{booking_id}}', the pager under the table reads 'Total 1 items', and the row's blue 'download confirmation slip' link in the 'Action' column is visible on screen.
blocks.terminate_criterion: A login or sign-in form is displayed instead of the Bingtrip merchant portal — this means the browser session was not authenticated (or its authenticated state did not survive), not that the workflow itself did anything wrong — or, after every filter field was cleared and 'Search' was clicked with only '{{booking_id}}' in the 'Booking ID' field, the results table is empty or contains no row matching '{{booking_id}}'.

data_schema.title: OrderRowDetails
data_schema.description: The values read from the single matching order row on the Orders > Booking Manage page.

ibn.title: Internal Booking Number (IBN)
ibn.description: The long hexadecimal PLATFORM BOOKING ID on the SECOND line of the 'Booking ID / Platform Booking ID' cell, copied verbatim (e.g. '5e977b32aaddd27f0be39daf2d0b8430'). Never return the shorter numeric Booking ID printed on the FIRST line of that same cell — that one is not the IBN. It is the same value that the downloaded voucher prints next to 'Booking No'. Output null if the cell is empty.

hcn.title: Hotel Confirmation Number (HCN)
hcn.description: The value in the 'Confirmation No' column of the row, copied verbatim (e.g. '32685SG107373'). This column sits to the right of 'Guest / Contact Person' and may require scrolling the table sideways to see. Output null if it is empty.

hotelName.title: Hotel Name
hotelName.description: The hotel name on the FIRST line of the 'Hotel Name / Room Type' cell, copied verbatim (e.g. 'Under Canvas Grand Canyon'). Do not include the room type printed underneath it.

roomCategory.title: Room Type
roomCategory.description: The room type on the SECOND line of the 'Hotel Name / Room Type' cell, copied verbatim (e.g. 'Suite with Kids Tent - Private Bath'). Keep the full text including any ' - ' separated qualifier. Do not include the hotel name printed above it, and do not add a room count.

checkinDate.title: Check-in Date
checkinDate.description: The check-in date, i.e. the part BEFORE the '~' on the first line of the 'Check-In/Out / Room Night' cell (e.g. from '2026-09-19 ~2026-09-21' take '2026-09-19'). It is already printed as ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DD — copy it as-is, no reformatting. Never use the 'Booking Date' column, which is when the order was placed, not a stay date.

checkoutDate.title: Check-out Date
checkoutDate.description: The check-out date, i.e. the part AFTER the '~' on the first line of the 'Check-In/Out / Room Night' cell (e.g. from '2026-09-19 ~2026-09-21' take '2026-09-21'), already in ISO-8601 YYYY-MM-DD form. Never use the 'Booking Date' column.

guestNames.title: Guest Names
guestNames.description: Every name listed on the FIRST line of the 'Guest / Contact Person' cell, split on commas, in the order printed, each copied VERBATIM in its original 'Surname/Firstname' form (e.g. 'DeMeij/Daniel'). KEEP DUPLICATES: this portal repeats the lead guest's name once per booked guest, so 'DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel' must be returned as four separate array items, not deduplicated to one — the number of entries is the only available indication of how many guests the booking covers. Do not reformat, reorder or translate the names, and never include the telephone number printed on the second line of the cell. Output null only if the cell has no names at all.

guestCount.title: Guest Count
guestCount.description: How many comma-separated names appear on the first line of the 'Guest / Contact Person' cell, counting repeated names separately (e.g. 'DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel,DeMeij/Daniel' -> 4). This is a cross-check on guestNames, so it must equal the number of items in that array. Output null if there are no names.

error_code_mapping.not_authenticated: A login or sign-in form is displayed — the browser session is not authenticated
error_code_mapping.booking_not_found: The results table after clearing all filters and searching by Booking ID contains no row matching '{{booking_id}}'

blocks.label: Download_Voucher
blocks.title: Download_Voucher
blocks.navigation_goal:
*** OBJECTIVE: get the voucher PDF for order '{{booking_id}}' ACTUALLY SAVED to disk ***

*** WHAT COUNTS AS DONE: a file was really downloaded. Clicking is not the same thing as downloading. On this portal a click on the download link can complete without any file being saved, and the page looks identical either way — so you CANNOT judge success by looking at the page. Judge it only by what the system reports back to you about the download after each action. ***

*** THE ONE RULE THAT MATTERS: if the system reports after your action that no file download was observed or credited, then the file was NOT saved. In that situation you must NOT report the goal complete — work through the recovery ladder below instead. Reporting complete there fails the whole workflow at the next step with nothing to parse. ***

### STEP 1 — CLICK
The results table already shows exactly one order row, the one matching '{{booking_id}}', and the previous block already scrolled the table so the 'Action' column is in view. If the 'Action' column is nevertheless off screen, drag the table's own horizontal scrollbar (immediately below the row) to the right until the blue 'download confirmation slip' link is visible. Then click that link.
- Do NOT click the 'Export' button above the table: it exports the order LIST as a spreadsheet, not the voucher. Do NOT click the refresh icon beside it.

### STEP 2 — DID A FILE ACTUALLY ARRIVE?
- If the system credits a download after the click, you are done: report the goal complete and stop. Do not click anything else.
- If the system reports that no download was observed or credited, go to the recovery ladder. Do not stop here.

### RECOVERY LADDER (in this order, stop as soon as a download is credited)
a) LOOK FOR A NEW BROWSER TAB. This portal may open the voucher in a second tab instead of downloading it, and a PDF shown in the browser's own viewer is NOT a downloaded file. If a new tab exists:
   - Switch to it. If it displays the PDF, click the download / save-arrow icon in the viewer's toolbar (top-right corner of the viewer) to save the file.
   - Then close that tab and switch back to the orders tab.
b) CLICK THE LINK AGAIN, once. A second click is allowed — and expected — when the first one produced no download. Never click it more than twice in total in this block.
c) After a second click, check again for a new tab and for a credited download, exactly as in (a).

### TERMINATE
- TERMINATE if the filtered results table with the row for '{{booking_id}}' is not present (e.g. a login form, an empty table, or an unrelated page) — this block assumes the previous block already filtered the list, and does not search for the booking itself.
- TERMINATE if the site answers a click with an error message that makes the download impossible.
- TERMINATE once you have worked the whole recovery ladder — two clicks, and a check for a new tab after each — and still no file has been saved. Do not report the goal complete in that case.

If a cookie-consent banner, toast or modal covers the link at any point, dismiss it and continue.

error_code_mapping.wrong_page: The filtered Booking Manage results table with the row for '{{booking_id}}' is not on screen, so the preceding navigation block did not actually reach it
error_code_mapping.download_not_available: The 'download confirmation slip' link was clicked but no file was ever saved - the site errored, or it rendered the voucher in the browser's PDF viewer instead of downloading it

blocks.label: Check_Download
blocks.code:
# Fail fast, and legibly, when the download block finished without saving a file.
# Skyvern hard-sets complete_on_download=True on file_download blocks, which turns OFF
# the completion verification pass — so the block reports success purely on the agent's
# own say-so, even when nothing landed on disk. Without this guard the run instead dies
# inside Extract_Data with an opaque "Failed to format jinja template / Can't compile
# non template nodes", because the file parser falls back to using the whole task-output
# dict as its file_url. Only downloaded_file_urls is interpolated here: it is a plain
# list of strings, whereas the full block output carries enum and datetime values whose
# repr is not valid Python.
file_urls = {{ Download_Voucher.downloaded_file_urls }}
if not isinstance(file_urls, list):
    file_urls = [file_urls] if file_urls else []
file_urls = [url for url in file_urls if isinstance(url, str) and url.strip()]

if not file_urls:
    raise Exception(
        "Download_Voucher finished without saving any file, so there is no voucher PDF for "
        "Extract_Data to parse. The click on 'download confirmation slip' did not produce a download "
        "the browser credited. Check the Download_Voucher block's recording for a second tab opening "
        "on the click: if the portal renders the voucher in the browser's built-in PDF viewer instead "
        "of sending it as an attachment, no download event fires and the file has to be saved from "
        "that viewer's own toolbar."
    )

return {"voucher_file_url": file_urls[0], "voucher_file_count": len(file_urls)}
blocks.prompt: Stop the run with a readable error when the voucher PDF was not actually downloaded.

extracted_information.description: The booking details read from the Bingtrip 'Voucher' PDF, as an array containing exactly one object. Always return exactly one item here, never zero and never more than one.

items.title: VoucherDetails
items.description: One booking's details read from the Bingtrip confirmation-slip ('Voucher') PDF.

address.title: Address
address.description: Full street address of the hotel. Source: the text printed to the right of the 'Address' label near the top of the voucher (e.g. 'WilliamsValle979 Airpark Lane', 'IstanbulSirkeci Eminonu FatihHudavendigar Caddesi No: 26'). This template concatenates city / district / street WITHOUT separating spaces — copy the string EXACTLY as printed, character for character; do not insert spaces or commas, do not reorder the parts, and do not try to tidy it into a conventional address. Output null if there is no 'Address' line.

phone.title: Phone
phone.description: The HOTEL's telephone number. Source: the text printed to the right of the 'Phone' label, directly under 'Address' (e.g. '1-928-2488808', '90-212-5121301'). Copy verbatim, keeping the hyphens exactly as printed. This is the only phone number in the document; never output the guest's or contact person's phone. Output null if there is no 'Phone' line.

bedType.title: Bed Type
bedType.description: Bed configuration. Source: the line printed under the 'Room info' label, copied verbatim (e.g. '1 King Bed and 1 Double Sofa Bed and 2 Twin Beds', '1 Double Bed and 1 Twin Bed'). Keep the whole string including every ' and ' separated part. Never take it from the room-type heading or from 'Meals'. Output null if there is no 'Room info' line or it is blank.

mealPlan.title: Meal Plan
mealPlan.description: Meal / board plan. Source: the line printed under the 'Meals' label, copied verbatim (e.g. 'No Breakfast', 'Includes 3 breakfasts'). Copy it as printed even when it means no meals are included — 'No Breakfast' is a real value, not a missing one. Output null only if there is no 'Meals' line at all.

voucherHotelName.title: Hotel Name As Printed On The Voucher
voucherHotelName.description: The hotel name as this PDF prints it: the large bold line directly beneath the 'Voucher' title and above the 'Address' label (e.g. 'Under Canvas Grand Canyon', 'Lalahan'). Copy verbatim. Note this line is a single non-wrapping line and may be cut off for long hotel names — return whatever is actually printed, do not complete or guess the rest. Output null if it is absent.

voucherRoomType.title: Room Type As Printed On The Voucher
voucherRoomType.description: The room type as this PDF prints it: the bold grey line in the lower half of the page, on the same row as 'Price Details' but in the right-hand column, directly above the 'Guest Names' label (e.g. 'Suite with Kids Tent - Private Bath', 'Superior Triple Room'). Copy verbatim; it is a single non-wrapping line that may be cut off for long room names. Output null if it is absent.

voucherBookingNo.title: Booking No As Printed On The Voucher
voucherBookingNo.description: The value printed to the right of the 'Booking No' label at the very TOP of the page, above the 'Voucher' title — a long hexadecimal string (e.g. '5e977b32aaddd27f0be39daf2d0b8430'). Copy verbatim. This is the platform booking id; never confuse it with the 'Confirmation No' printed in blue further down the page. Output null if the 'Booking No' line is absent.

voucherConfirmationNo.title: Confirmation No As Printed On The Voucher
voucherConfirmationNo.description: The value printed in blue under the 'Confirmation No' heading in the middle band of the page (e.g. '32685SG107373', '9143799'). Copy verbatim. Never take the value printed next to 'Booking No' at the very top of the page — that is the platform's own booking id (a long hexadecimal string), not a confirmation number. Output null if the 'Confirmation No' block is empty.

blocks.label: Standardize_Output

workflow_definition.workflow_system_prompt:
You are parsing a hotel-reservation confirmation slip — titled 'Voucher' — issued by the Bingtrip merchant portal (bingtrip.com), downloaded from an order row via its 'download confirmation slip' link. The text you receive is the literal text layer of that PDF.

### HOW THIS WORKFLOW USES THE DOCUMENT
This is the SECOND of two parsing stages. The first stage already read the hotel name, room type, check-in/check-out dates, guest names, booking number and confirmation number straight from the portal's order table, because this PDF lays every value out as a SINGLE LINE THAT DOES NOT WRAP: when a value is too long for the page it is silently cut off rather than continued on the next line. So this stage must supply only the fields the order table does not show — the address, the hotel phone number, the bed configuration and the meal plan — plus a few already-known values that are re-read here as cross-checks and fallbacks (the 'Booking No' at the top of the page is the same platform booking id the order table shows on the second line of its 'Booking ID / Platform Booking ID' cell). Never try to reconstruct or complete a line that looks truncated: return exactly the characters that are printed.

### DOCUMENT LAYOUT
A single framed page of plain 'label / value' pairs, top to bottom:
- 'Booking No' followed by a long hexadecimal string — the PLATFORM's booking id (the value typed into the portal's Booking ID filter). It is not the shorter numeric booking number and not a confirmation number.
- The 'Voucher' title, then the hotel name in large bold type, then 'Address' and 'Phone' rows.
- A three-column band: 'Confirmation No' (printed in blue) | 'Check in' / 'Check out' (printed as an abbreviated month and day only, e.g. 'Sep 19' — WITH NO YEAR, plus the weekday and the 'After 15:00' / 'Before 10:00' desk times) | 'Rooms' and 'Nights' counts.
- A lower band: 'Price Details' with the order status and total amount on the left; on the right the room type in bold grey, then 'Guest Names', then 'Room info' (the bed configuration), then 'Meals' (the board basis).
- A 'Cancellation Policy' section at the bottom.

### RULES
1. Never invent a value. If a field is not literally present in the text, output null.
2. Copy every text value VERBATIM: original spelling, casing, punctuation and spacing. This template concatenates address parts without separating spaces (e.g. 'WilliamsValle979 Airpark Lane') — reproduce that exactly; do not insert spaces, do not reorder, do not tidy, do not translate.
3. Never substitute one field for another: 'Booking No' is the platform booking id, never the confirmation number; the room type is never the hotel name; 'Room info' is the bed configuration, never the meal plan.
4. 'No Breakfast' under 'Meals' is a real, meaningful value — output it, do not treat it as a missing field.
5. Do not read the check-in/check-out dates from this document as final values: they carry no year, so the workflow takes the dates from the portal page instead.
